title: Osso Buco
description:
Osso Buco is one the great “comfort foods,” especially during those long and chilly Winter months when you need to spend more time staying warm inside. It’s the perfect time to do this slow-cooked veal.
Osso Buco means “bone with a hole” and it refers to a cross-cut veal shank with marrow in the center of the bone. Some people are a little squeamish about eating this, but when it’s cooked in this dish, it’s delicious (and always good for you).
The classic side dish for Osso Buco is Risotto Milanese.
ingredients: 4 center-cut slices of veal shank, each about 1 ½ inches thick, tied around with a string
Heat 3 tablespoons oil in a deep, heavy oven-proof pot that has a lid.
directions: Mix the flour with a generous helping of salt and some pepper. Dredge the veal shanks in the flour, on both sides, and shake off any excess.
When the oil is hot, but not smoking, put the veal shanks in and sear until nicely browned, about 3 minutes per side. Remove from the pot and set aside.
Add the remaining oil, along with the onion, carrot, celery, garlic, bay leaves, and a little salt. Cook until golden, stirring occasionally, about 8 minutes.
Pour in the white wine and stir and scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze it. Cook until the wine is reduced by half, about 5 minutes.
Add the beef stock and cook until the liquid is reduced by half, another 5 minutes.
Put the drained plum tomatoes into the pot, together with the thyme, rosemary, and a little more salt. Break up the tomatoes with the back of a spoon. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes.
Return the veal shanks to the pot. If the tomato mixture doesn’t come up to about two thirds of the height of the shanks, add some more water, or beef broth, or the drained tomato juice.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and braise in the oven for about 2 hours, carefully turning the shanks every 30 minutes.
When the veal is done, it should be very tender, with the meat almost falling off the bone. Put the shanks on a platter and cover with foil until ready to serve.
Add the mushrooms to the sauce and cook over moderately high heat until the sauce is reduced a bit, about 10 minutes. Adjust the seasonings.
Make the gremolata by mixing the lemon zest, garlic, and parsley in a small bowl.
To serve, remove the strings from the veal shanks and cover generously with the sauce. Sprinkle with the gremolata.
